descriptors.concept_name: Taxation Regime of Special Entities and Non-Profit Organisations
descriptors.definition: This chapter covers the income tax treatment and exemptions applicable to educational and medical organizations, charitable or religious trusts, political parties, electoral trusts, and special entities like securitization trusts, business trusts, and investment funds under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Specific provisions govern registered non-profit organizations and special investment vehicles through dedicated sections and schedules.
inclusion: Charitable and religious institutions
Educational and medical organizations
Political parties and electoral trusts
Securitization and business trusts
Investment funds
exclusion: Standard corporate entities not falling under special exemptions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general commercial entities and special tax-exempt non-profit or pass-through vehicles.

descriptors.concept_name: Exemption for Certain Educational and Medical Institutions
descriptors.definition: Specific universities, educational institutions, hospitals, and medical institutions are exempt from income tax on their total income if they are wholly or substantially financed by the government, or if their aggregate annual receipts do not exceed five crore rupees. An institution is considered substantially financed when government grants exceed 50 percent of its total receipts including donations during the tax year.
inclusion: Universities wholly or substantially financed by the government
Hospitals existing solely for philanthropic purposes and substantially financed by the government
Educational and medical institutions with aggregate annual receipts not exceeding five crore rupees
exclusion: Hospitals or educational institutions exceeding the financial receipt threshold without government financing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes government-backed or smaller scale medical and educational bodies from standard commercial enterprises and general trusts.

descriptors.concept_name: Special Provisions for Registered Non-Profit Organization
descriptors.definition: Non-profit organizations are typically established as trusts, societies, or section 8 companies to carry out charitable or religious activities. A trust involves an obligation where a trustee holds and manages property according to a trust deed for the benefit of ascertainable or unascertainable beneficiaries.
inclusion: Trusts, societies, and section 8 companies
Public trusts with general public beneficiaries
Private trusts formed for individual or family convenience
exclusion: Commercial business entities operating for profit
Private trusts claiming public charitable exemptions solely by status
nearby_distinctions: Public trusts qualify for special charitable exemption regimes, whereas private trusts do not qualify merely by being constituted as a trust.

descriptors.definition: Discretionary trusts, where income is not specifically receivable on behalf of a single person or individual shares are indeterminate, are generally taxed at the maximum marginal rate. Specific statutory exceptions apply under conditions such as will-created trusts, certain dependent relative trusts, and employee benefit funds.
inclusion: Trusts with unknown or indeterminate beneficiary shares
Representative assessees managing property under court orders or trust deeds
exclusion: Trusts with specific, determinate beneficiary shares
Exempt provident, superannuation, or gratuity funds meeting specific conditions
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts with determinate trusts where beneficiary shares are known and taxed accordingly rather than at the maximum marginal rate.

descriptors.concept_name: Special Provisions Relating to Income of Political Parties and Electoral Trusts
descriptors.definition: Political parties and electoral trusts receive tax exemptions on specific categories of income such as house property, other sources, capital gains, and voluntary contributions. To claim this exemption, entities must maintain proper books of accounts, record large contributions, audit accounts via a chartered accountant, and file required statutory returns.
inclusion: Income from house property of political parties
Voluntary contributions received by political parties and electoral trusts
Capital gains and income from other sources for political bodies
exclusion: Income failing to meet record-keeping and audit criteria
Donations accepted outside prescribed banking or electronic channels beyond permitted limits
nearby_distinctions: Exempts political and electoral income only upon strict compliance with transparency and record-keeping mandates, unlike standard trust income.

descriptors.concept_name: Taxation Regime for Securitization Trusts and its Investors
descriptors.definition: Securitization involves converting future cash flows from loans or receivables into marketable securities through a special purpose trust or vehicle. The trust acquires these assets from an originator and issues securitized debt instruments to investors while distributing incoming borrower repayments.
instrument_references: Securities and Exchange Board of India Regulations, 2008
inclusion: Special purpose distinct entities under SEBI regulations
Special purpose vehicles regulated by RBI guidelines on securitization
Trusts set up by securitization or reconstruction companies under the SARFAESI Act
exclusion: Standard corporate entities not engaged in asset-backed securitization
nearby_distinctions: Differs from standard business trusts by specifically dealing with the acquisition and refinancing of debt pools and receivables.

descriptors.concept_name: Scheme for Taxation of Real Estate Investment Trust and Infrastructure Investment Trust
descriptors.definition: Real Estate Investment Trusts and Infrastructure Investment Trusts are investment vehicles set up as trusts and registered with SEBI to hold assets for the benefit of unit holders. REITs must invest the majority of their asset value in completed, rent-generating properties while adhering to strict listing and investment thresholds.
inclusion: Real Estate Investment Trusts
Infrastructure Investment Trusts
Freehold or leasehold commercial real estate assets
exclusion: Unlisted investment vehicles failing mandatory stock exchange requirements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from securitization trusts by focusing on direct or indirect ownership of physical real estate and infrastructure assets rather than loan receivables.

descriptors.concept_name: Special Taxation Regime for Investment Funds and Income Received from Such Funds
descriptors.definition: Income received by a unit holder from an investment fund is taxed as if the underlying investments were made directly by the unit holder. Investment funds are generally exempt from tax on income other than profits and gains from business or profession, which remains taxable at the fund level.
terminology: Profits and gains from business or profession
inclusion: Income distributed by investment funds to resident and non-resident unit holders
Business income taxable directly at the investment fund level
exclusion: Offshore investment income routed through specified alternative investment funds for non-residents under direct investment rules
nearby_distinctions: Pass-through taxation applies to non-business incomes of investment funds, whereas business profits are taxed directly at the fund level.
